| Aspect | SQLite | PostgreSQL |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Architecture | Embedded database stored in a single file inside your app process; no server to install, configure, or secure | Full client-server database; a separate service to run or pay for, with connection management and network latency |
| Operations | Trivial deployment; backup is copying the file | Managed offerings make operations easy, but there is more to run than with SQLite |
| Performance (small app) | Very fast reads with no network hop; WAL mode handles many concurrent readers well | Strong concurrency via MVCC, with many simultaneous writers |
| Writes | Single writer at a time | Many concurrent writers |
| Features | Fewer built-in types and features; limited `ALTER TABLE`; no native user/role management | Rich types (JSONB, arrays, full-text search), extensions like PostGIS, robust constraints, fine-grained access control |
| Scaling | Awkward with multiple app servers, since the file must sit on one machine's local disk | Scales from a small app to a large one without a migration |
| Best fit | One server, light write load, minimal ops | Multiple app instances, heavy concurrent writes, or advanced features needed from the start |
